brief.subject: Family Dollar to pay $63 million over checkout overcharges
brief.headline: Family Dollar Settles Overcharge Claims for $63 Million; FTC Sues Over Vet Supply Deal
brief.dek: Regulators target register prices above shelf tags and a vet-supply merger they say could raise pet care costs.
brief.lede: Family Dollar will pay $63 million to settle FTC and state allegations that it charged shoppers more at the register than its posted prices.

sections.heading: Family Dollar's $63 Million Price Settlement
bullets: The FTC and 17 states reached a $63 million settlement with Family Dollar Stores.
Regulators allege the chain routinely rang up prices above those on shelves, price tags and ads.
The alleged overcharges cost consumers millions of dollars, which makes checking receipts against shelf prices worthwhile.
Officials frame the deal as a win for price transparency at the checkout.

sections.heading: FTC Moves to Block Vet Supply Merger
bullets: The FTC sued to stop Covetrus from buying rival MWI Veterinary Supply in a $3.5 billion deal.
The agency says the two are the biggest distributors of veterinary products and services.
The FTC argues a merger would push up costs for clinics and, ultimately, for pet owners.

brief.seo_description: Family Dollar settles overcharge claims with the FTC and 17 states for $63 million, and the FTC sues to block a $3.5 billion vet-supply merger.
